meta.title: Future Perfect Tenses
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Future Perfect Tenses themed around mobile gaming.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Future Perfect tense paired with topics like passive voice, conditionals, relative clauses, gerunds, quantifiers, inversion, and more, all within familiar mobile game contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the server maintenance ends, the new patch _____ to all regions.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with the passive voice. The action will be completed before a specific future time ('By the time... ends'), and the subject receives the action.
explanation.concept: Completed future actions in the passive voice
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have been + past participle
examples: By tomorrow, the update will have been installed on all devices.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with a First Conditional structure. The 'if' clause requires the present simple tense, and the plural subject 'developers' requires the base verb 'release'.
explanation.concept: Present simple in 'if' clauses predicting a future perfect result
explanation.formula: If + plural subject + base verb, subject + will have + past participle
examples: If they announce the event today, we will have prepared by tomorrow.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The guild, which _____ the raid boss by midnight, will claim the exclusive rewards.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with a non-defining relative clause. 'Will have farmed' indicates an action that will be completed before a specific future time ('by midnight').
explanation.concept: Future Perfect in relative clauses describing completion before a future point
explanation.formula: Noun, which + will have + past participle + by + future time, + will + base verb
examples: The team, which will have finished the project by Friday, will celebrate.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with gerund verb patterns. The verb 'finish' must be followed by a gerund ('grinding'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Verbs requiring gerund complements in Future Perfect contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will have + finished + verb-ing
examples: She will have finished reading the guide by tonight.

data.hint: Choose the correct quantifiers to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the end of the season, _____ players will have spent a significant amount of gems, while _____ will have reached the top rank.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with quantifiers. 'Players' is a countable plural noun, requiring 'many'. The implied noun for the second blank is also countable ('players'), requiring 'few'.
explanation.concept: Countable quantifiers with Future Perfect subjects
explanation.formula: Many + plural noun + will have + past participle; few + will have + past participle
examples: Many users will have upgraded, but few will have mastered it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This question contains no errors. It correctly combines the Future Perfect tense with an adverbial clause of time and a prepositional phrase ('depending on').
explanation.concept: Correct usage of Future Perfect with time clauses and prepositions
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have + past participle + depending on + noun
examples: By the time the match ends, they will have distributed prizes depending on the score.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: Rarely _____ such a generous login bonus before the anniversary event concludes.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with negative adverbial inversion. 'Rarely' at the beginning of the sentence triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('will the developers have released').
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative adverbs in Future Perfect
explanation.formula: Rarely + will + subject + have + past participle
examples: Never will the system have processed so many requests.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with subject-verb agreement rules. 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('will have'), and 'a number of' takes a plural verb ('will have', not 'will has').
explanation.concept: Agreement with 'the number of' vs. 'a number of' in Future Perfect
explanation.formula: The number of + noun + will have + past participle; a number of + noun + will have + been + past participle
examples: The number of errors will have dropped, while a number of issues will have been resolved.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the new season begins, the current meta _____ significantly.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with an adverbial clause of time. 'Will have shifted' indicates an action that will be completed before the future event ('the new season begins').
explanation.topic: Future Perfect + Adverbial Clauses of Time
explanation.concept: Future Perfect for actions completed before a future time marker
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have + past participle
examples: By the time the movie starts, we will have arrived.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: By the end of the tournament,

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with modal verbs of deduction in the perfect form. Modal verbs ('must') are always followed by the base form 'have', never 'has'.
explanation.concept: Base form of 'have' after modal verbs in perfect constructions
explanation.formula: Subject + must + have + past participle; subject + will have + past participle
examples: He must have trained for months, and he will have perfected his strategy.

data.hint: Choose the correct discourse marker to complete the sentence.
data.question: The game has been struggling with server issues; _____, by next month, the company will have upgraded its infrastructure.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous with the Future Perfect tense and a resultative discourse marker. 'Therefore' correctly links the ongoing problem with the future solution.
explanation.concept: Using resultative discourse markers with Future Perfect contexts
explanation.formula: Present perfect continuous clause; therefore, + subject + will have + past participle
examples: The system is outdated; therefore, we will have replaced it by Friday.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with a cleft sentence for emphasis. 'It is' is required for singular emphasis on 'the dedicated players'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in it-cleft structures with Future Perfect
explanation.formula: It + is + plural noun + who + will have + past participle
examples: It is the developers who will have fixed the bugs by tomorrow.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ for weeks, the player will have maxed out their character's level by the time the new expansion launches.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect participle clause with the Future Perfect tense. 'Having ground' (past participle of grind) indicates an action completed before the main Future Perfect action.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle indicating an action prior to the Future Perfect main verb
explanation.formula: Having + past participle, subject + will have + past participle + by the time + present simple
examples: Having studied all night, she will have mastered the material by the exam.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: By the end of the month,

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with advanced comparatives. 'Popular' is a multi-syllable adjective, so it requires 'more popular', not 'more popularer' (which is a double comparative error).
explanation.concept: Correct comparative forms in Future Perfect sentences
explanation.formula: Subject + will have + become + more + adjective + than + noun
examples: The app will have become more efficient than the old version.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the maintenance is over, the devs will have _____ the controversial changes and _____ the servers back online.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with phrasal verbs. After 'will have', both phrasal verbs must be in their past participle forms ('rolled back', 'brought').
explanation.concept: Past participle forms of phrasal verbs in Future Perfect
explanation.formula: Subject + will have + past participle of phrasal verb + and + past participle of phrasal verb
examples: They will have shut down the system and restarted it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it correctly takes the indefinite article 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Indefinite articles before words starting with a /j/ sound
explanation.formula: Subject + will have + released + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: They will have built a unique platform by then.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the elliptical sentence.
data.question: The veterans will have mastered the new mechanics by tomorrow, but the newcomers _____.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with ellipsis. The auxiliary 'won't have' is used to avoid repeating the full Future Perfect verb phrase ('will have mastered').
explanation.concept: Omitting repeated verb phrases in Future Perfect using auxiliary verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + will have + past participle, but + subject + won't have
examples: She will have finished her work, but I won't have.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a past unreal conditional ('If only... had listened') with a Third Conditional main clause. The result of a past unreal condition requires 'would have avoided', not 'will have avoided'.
explanation.concept: Correct modal usage in hypothetical past conditionals
explanation.formula: If only + subject + had + past participle, subject + would have + past participle
examples: If only I had studied, I would have passed the exam.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Not only _____ the update introduced new characters, but it _____ also rebalanced the existing roster.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with 'not only... but also' inversion. 'Not only' triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('will the update have introduced'), and the second clause uses 'will have' to maintain the Future Perfect tense.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'not only' in Future Perfect
explanation.formula: Not only + will + subject + have + past participle, but + subject + will + also + have + past participle
examples: Not only will she have finished the report, but she will also have presented it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect passive with negative adverbial inversion. 'Under no circumstances' at the beginning of a clause requires subject-auxiliary inversion ('will the account have').
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative phrases in Future Perfect
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + will + subject + have + been + past participle
examples: Under no circumstances will the data have been compromised.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ assistance, the support team will have already prepared a comprehensive guide by the time you contact them.

explanation.text: This combines first conditional inversion ('Should you need') with the Future Perfect tense in the main clause to describe an action completed before another future action.
explanation.concept: Inversion with 'should' for future possibility paired with Future Perfect
explanation.formula: Should + subject + base verb, subject + will have + past participle + by the time + present simple
examples: Should you require help, we will have already prepared the documents.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the mandative subjunctive with a future time clause. After 'insist that', the verb must be in the base form ('be'), not the Future Perfect 'will have been'.
explanation.concept: Mandative subjunctive overriding Future Perfect in 'insist that' clauses
explanation.formula: Subject + insist + that + subject + base verb + before + present simple
examples: They insist that the system be updated before it launches.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The new update will have been so transformative that it will seem as though the game _____ entirely rebuilt.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect passive with 'as though' + past subjunctive ('were') to describe an unreal or hypothetical comparison resulting from the future action.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Past subjunctive for unreal comparisons following Future Perfect
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + so + adjective + that + it will seem as though + subject + were + past participle
examples: The renovation will have been so complete that it will seem as though the house were new.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

correctAnswers: will the new gameplay loop have

multiErrorSegments.text: on it by the end of the week.

explanation.text: This combines 'so + adjective' inversion with the Future Perfect tense. The correct inversion is 'will the new gameplay loop have become', placing the auxiliary 'will' before the subject and 'have' after it.
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'so' in Future Perfect
explanation.formula: So + adjective + will + subject + have + past participle + that + clause
examples: So difficult will the test have been that students will have struggled.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: What the community does not realize is that the developers _____ already _____ the next three seasons by the end of this month.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with a noun clause acting as the subject complement. 'Will have planned' indicates an action completed before a specific future time.
explanation.concept: Future Perfect in noun clauses following present tense verbs
explanation.formula: What + subject + present simple verb + is that + subject + will have + past participle + by + future time
examples: What they don't know is that we will have already finished by Friday.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with verb patterns. 'Expect' is followed by a perfect infinitive ('to have recruited') to refer to a future completed action, not a gerund.
explanation.concept: Perfect infinitives following 'expect' to indicate future completion
explanation.formula: Subject + expects + to have + past participle + by + future time, meaning + subject + will have + past participle
examples: She expects to have finished the project by Monday, meaning she will have met the deadline.

data.hint: Choose the correct prepositions to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the end of the event, the players will be accustomed _____ the new mechanics, and the developers will have been responsive _____ their feedback.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with preposition collocations. 'Accustomed' is followed by 'to', and 'responsive' is also followed by 'to'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific adjectives in Future Perfect contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will be accustomed to + noun; subject + will have been responsive to + noun
examples: They will be accustomed to the rules, and the staff will have been responsive to complaints.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with sequence of tenses and subject-verb agreement. The plural subject 'creators' requires the plural auxiliary 'will have', not 'will has'.
explanation.concept: Plural agreement in compound Future Perfect sentences
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have + past participle, and + plural subject + will have + past participle
examples: By the time the company expands, it will have grown, and the founders will have stepped down.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: It is widely expected that the new expansion _____ by millions of players before the end of the year.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with passive reporting structures. 'Will have been downloaded' indicates a future completed action in the passive voice.
explanation.concept: Future Perfect passive in reporting structures
explanation.formula: It is expected that + subject + will have been + past participle + by + future time
examples: It is believed that the bridge will have been completed by December.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This question contains no errors. It correctly combines the Future Perfect tense with an adverbial clause of time, using the present simple 'notice' in the time clause and 'will have adjusted' in the main clause.
explanation.concept: Present simple in future time clauses with Future Perfect main clauses
explanation.formula: By the time + subject + present simple, subject + will have + already + past participle
examples: By the time you arrive, we will have already started.
